title: Microbiologist Salary Guide: Hourly to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Convert your microbiologist salary from hourly to annual pay using a 38-hour week. Includes tax, super, casual loading, and fortnightly estimates.
salarySummary: Based on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, a full-time microbiologist working 38 hours per week would earn $1004.90 per week, but actual salaries for professional scientists are typically higher, with ABS average full-time earnings around $2083.70 per week.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary for a microbiologist role?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, annual pay would be $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.88 before tax and super. If you are a casual employee, add 25% casual loading, making the rate $33.05 per hour, giving $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,318.80. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool for any rate.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading for a microbiologist, and how does it affect pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. For a microbiologist earning the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour. This loading applies to award/agreement-free employees. If you are covered by an award, check the specific rate. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how to calculate it correctly.

faqs.q: How much superannuation should I expect on my microbiologist salary?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your salary. For a full-time microbiologist earning $1004.90 per week, super would be $120.59 per week, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional contribution by your employer. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Microbiologist Salary in Australia

If you are a microbiologist or considering a career in microbiology, knowing how to convert your hourly rate to an annual salary is essential for budgeting and comparing job offers. This guide uses the standard 38-hour week and a 52-week year to help you calculate your pay, including tax and superannuation. We rely on official sources such as the Fair Work Commission, the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS), and the Australian Taxation Office.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 for a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This is the base rate for adult employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, a microbiologist salary is typically higher because most microbiologists are professionals covered by awards or enterprise agreements. According to Jobs and Skills Australia, microbiologists are classified under Life Scientists (ANZSCO 234517) and usually hold a bachelor degree or higher. The ABS does not publish a specific median weekly earnings figure for microbiologists, but for all full-time adult non-managerial employees, the average weekly ordinary time earnings are $2,083.70 (May 2026). This equates to approximately $54.83 per hour for a 38-hour week. Your actual microbiologist salary will depend on your experience, employer, and location.

### Converting Hourly to Annual: The Formula

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, use the formula:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a 38-hour week, which is the standard full-time week used by the Fair Work Commission. For example, if your hourly rate is $50.00, your annual pay would be $50.00 × 38 × 52 = $98,800. This is before tax and super. If you are paid fortnightly, multiply your weekly pay by 2: $50.00 × 38 = $1,900 per week, so $3,800 per fortnight. Use our [the timesheet](/) to calculate your own figures.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you work as a casual microbiologist, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base rate. The Fair Work Ombudsman states that a casual employee aged 21 or over should get at least $33.05 per hour (including loading). For a casual microbiologist earning $33.05 per hour, the annual gross pay would be $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,318.80. Remember, casual loading is added to the base rate; never type a rate that already includes loading into our calculator.

Superannuation is paid on top of your salary. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a full-time microbiologist earning $1,900 per week, super would be $228 per week. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra contribution by your employer. See our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page for more details.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds). For a microbiologist earning $98,800 per year, the tax would be approximately $22,867 plus Medicare of $1,976, leaving a take-home pay of about $73,957 per year, or $1,422 per week. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a precise estimate.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Breakdown

Knowing your fortnightly pay helps with budgeting. Simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For a $50 per hour rate: $1,900 per week = $3,800 per fortnight. This is useful for rent or loan repayments. Our [pay guides](/blog) offer more tips on managing your pay cycle.

### Comparing Microbiologist Salaries

While the ABS does not provide a specific median for microbiologists, the average weekly earnings for all full-time employees in professional, scientific and technical services (a common industry for microbiologists) is a useful benchmark. According to the ABS Survey of Employee Earnings and Hours (May 2025), the median weekly earnings for full-time non-managerial life scientists may be higher than the national average due to the high level of education required. Jobs and Skills Australia notes that 41.2% of microbiologists hold a postgraduate qualification and 51% hold a bachelor degree. This typically leads to higher pay. You can explore more industry data on our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.

### Important Disclaimer

Annual pay calculated here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

### Next Steps

To get a personalised estimate of your microbiologist salary, enter your hourly rate into our [the timesheet](/) calculator. Check the casual loading box if applicable. You can also refer to our [reference tables](/data) for award rates and [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) updates. For job-specific pay, see our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) guide.
